html:
SMTO-EXE-0093 — SMTO can only save screenshots as PNG or JPEG

GUID: 03413967-3a74-5b9b-8caf-f7d08f53e79a
Slug: screen-unsupported-format
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to save a screenshot as a file type it doesn't make. It only makes PNG or JPEG pictures, so nothing was captured.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO again for the screenshot as a PNG (best quality) or a JPEG (smaller file). These are the only two picture types SMTO's screen tools can save.
  2. If you want a JPEG at a set quality, pick a number from 1 to 95. SMTO refuses JPEG quality values outside that range.
  3. If you need another file type, such as WebP or PDF, convert the PNG after SMTO saves it. SMTO can't make other types directly, but a saved PNG can be converted without losing detail.

What success looks like

  • SMTO saves the screenshot as a PNG or JPEG and attaches it to the task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it, with the file type you asked for, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Screenshot validation or encoding received a format other than png or jpeg.

What this means

  • Screenshot validation or encoding received a format other than the supported png or jpeg values. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Screenshot validation or encoding received a format other than the supported png or jpeg values.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the requested format and any JPEG quality setting under the advertised schema.

How to fix it

  • screen_contract.validate and protocol.encode_image accept format 'png' or 'jpeg' only. jpeg_quality must be an integer from 1 to 95 and is only accepted together with format 'jpeg'.
  • Request png or jpeg with JPEG quality between 1 and 95.

Retry and execution caution

  • Request png or jpeg with JPEG quality between 1 and 95.

How to verify the fix

  • A png or jpeg request with valid quality produces the intended artifact.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
